speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the pain migrated to the right lower quadrant, and is it currently severe enough that movement worsens it? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Lactate Level. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Pelvic_CXR_and_CTA.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The requested tests (Complete Blood Count and Lactate Level) and images (Abdominal_Pelvic_CXR and CTA) were not provided in the available data; however, the patient's abdominal examination reveals a bruit heard over the epigastric area, mild periumbilical tenderness, and imaging from a CT Angiography of the abdomen indicates evidence suggestive of reduced blood flow to the mesenteric arteries.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known diabetes mellitus for 35 years and hypertension for 20 years. History of acute myocardial infarction. Social history: Smokes 15–20 cigarettes per day for the past 40 years.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, vomiting. Reports bloody loose bowel movements. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ischemic Colitis. The patient's age, history of recent myocardial infarction, sudden onset of left-sided/bloody diarrhea, and the previous incorrect migraine diagnosis suggest compromised blood flow to the colon. Please confirm if the pain is located in the lower abdomen and if you have any history of atrial fibrillation.
